subject.title: Feature Request: Gateway lifecycle hooks (onSubagentComplete, onToolCallThreshold, onTurnComplete)

question: Should OpenClaw expose subagent completion, agent turn completion, and tool-call threshold boundaries through HOOK.md workspace/internal hooks, typed plugin hooks only, or a split surface with different payload and authority levels?
rationale: The source gap is proven, but the correct API affects trusted local code execution, session-state exposure, hook ordering, possible threshold config, and the boundary between workspace automation and plugin middleware.

options.title: Split Observation From Control
options.body: Expose only minimized observation-oriented workspace events first, while keeping richer result, mutation, threshold, and policy behavior in typed plugin hooks.

options.title: Use Typed Plugin Hooks Only
options.body: Do not add new HOOK.md lifecycle events; instead extend typed plugin APIs for lifecycle and receipt use cases that need stronger contracts.

options.title: Design Broader Hook API First
options.body: Keep this issue as the lifecycle-hook umbrella until related hook requests are reconciled into one API proposal.

recommendation.title: Split Observation From Control
recommendation.body: Expose only minimized observation-oriented workspace events first, while keeping richer result, mutation, threshold, and policy behavior in typed plugin hooks.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans product shape, security posture, and hook authority boundaries, and the issue discussion already routed this topic to steipete.
